$comment: EXPECTED SURFACE DELTA — the committed manifest of every difference between the workbench surface captured from origin/main (8a4bd011) and the tree under test. It is EMPTY, and empty is the STEADY STATE: main does not differ from its own baseline.

Checked by: `npm run check:surface-baseline` (node scripts/capture-surface-baseline.mjs compare --baseline src/modules/workbench/core/__fixtures__/surface-baseline.main.json), which runs inside `npm run check`. Re-capture with `npm run capture:surface-baseline`.

THE CONTRACT. A difference NOT listed here fails the comparison. An entry listed here that does NOT materialise ALSO fails it, so a stale allowance cannot silently widen the gate. A branch that legitimately changes the workbench surface declares each difference here with facet / kind / name / an authorising `item` / a `disposition` / a `why`. A merge that lands such a change RE-CAPTURES the baseline and empties this list again, in the SAME commit — the manifest is a transit record, not an accumulating ledger.

disposition: deleted = gone from the tree entirely | relocated = re-exported by extensions/index.ts (VERIFIED against that barrel) | unexported = still exported by some workbench module, just not by the public barrel (VERIFIED against the module-export set) | relocated-installer = registered by a different installer but still reachable from the canonical mount path (VERIFIED against widgetKinds) | renamed / added / moved = self-describing.

ALLOWANCE SCOPE — TWO narrowings, because neither alone is enough. The viewSpecs facet compares the PARSED + LOWERED form of both shipping ui/*.yaml at JSON-Pointer granularity, and `pointerDiff` reports the SHALLOWEST differing path. (1) CONTENT-BINDING: a viewSpecs allowance MUST carry the `detail` string of the difference it permits, and it is matched — so an allowance is a permit for ONE observed change, not for a path. This binds at EVERY depth, which the depth rule alone cannot, since the allowance key is facet:kind:name and ignores content. Its RESIDUAL is real and stated: `detail` is truncated at 200 chars, so two changes to a large subtree agreeing on the first 200 characters are indistinguishable to it. (2) DEPTH: an allowance at pointer depth <= 2 (`cell-filter/checks`, `qc/canvas`, …) covers a whole section or list element — exactly where that truncation bites — so it must additionally say "blanket": true out loud. A genuine wholesale change stays declarable; it cannot be written by accident, and it is visible in review.

ARRAY IDENTITY (ITEM-P1, 2026-08-10). Arrays whose elements carry an authored `id` — widgets, checks, actions, canvas/datasets, canvas/series — are compared BY THAT ID and their pointer segment is `#<id>`, not the index. Before this, elements were compared POSITIONALLY, so inserting one widget at index N reported every later sibling as changed: measured on this very list, the single `unreadableColumnsAlert` insertion demanded 72 allowances (71 renumbering + 1 blanket for the shifted trailing element) where it now demands 1. A 72-entry manifest is not a stricter gate, it is one nobody reads — the blanket-permit failure of the pre-recapture device arrived at from the other direction — and it made every widget insertion an expensive, conflict-prone edit to a live merge hotspot. The rule is structural, not a list of key names: every element an object with a non-empty string `id`, unique within its array. Anything else (columns, parts, body, switchTo, arrays of primitives, duplicated ids, mixed arrays) keeps the positional rule. NOTHING ABOVE IS WEAKENED: `#`-segments are RFC-6901 escaped and sit at the depth their index did, so the depth<=2 blanket rule fires identically; content-binding is untouched; and because keying by id would otherwise make render ORDER invisible, the order of the surviving elements is compared in its own right and a reorder is reported at the array itself.

RE-CAPTURED 2026-08-10 AT main 8a4bd011, AND WHAT THAT RETIRED. Until this entry the baseline was a real worktree at 06d99c65 — the PRE-`processor-ui-language` tree shape — and this manifest carried 602 item-attributed allowances. Together they were the INV-4 BEFORE/AFTER EQUIVALENCE ARGUMENT: that a round which deleted ~10,600 lines added no capability and changed no behaviour. THAT ARGUMENT IS RETIRED. This file no longer makes it, the baseline can no longer support it, and no prose here should be read as if it did.

WHY IT HAD TO GO — measured, not supposed. A brand-new, schema-valid `check` inserted into the shipped cell-filter.yaml produced 602 differences and ZERO UNEXPECTED: the gate could not see it. 28 of the 257 viewSpecs allowances sat at pointer depth <= 2 (cell-filter/checks, cell-filter/layout, cell-filter/data/obsSources, qc/canvas, qc/derived, qc/const/presets, ...), and every one of those was a standing permit over an entire subtree. Independently, main had advanced 621 commits past 06d99c65, so the manifest had grown `carried-in: <sha>` allowances for main's OWN work — a snapshot that can no longer tell you WHOSE change a difference is has stopped being an equivalence argument whatever its depth profile.

WHAT THE DEVICE GUARANTEES NOW. The baseline is captured from current main in the SAME tree shape as the tree under test; EMPTY is this list's steady state (it carries exactly the differences the branch under test declares, and a merge re-captures it back to empty); the 28 blanket permits are 0 and the scope rules above stop them coming back. The claim is no longer "this refactor preserved behaviour". It is: THIS TREE'S WORKBENCH SURFACE DOES NOT DIFFER FROM MAIN'S EXCEPT WHERE DECLARED HERE, EACH DIFFERENCE IS ATTRIBUTED TO AN AUTHORISING ITEM (enforced by the comparison itself, not merely by a test — a {facet,kind,name} triple with no `item` used to pass while the gate printed "item-attributed"), AND EVERY relocated / unexported / relocated-installer CLAIM IS VERIFIED AGAINST THE TREE RATHER THAN BELIEVED. Facets DIFFED: the public barrel's runtime + declared exports, the extensions barrel (a published entry point in its own right, so losing a contract from it fails like losing one from core), CONTRIBUTION_KINDS, PANE_KINDS, both widget-installer registries, and both shipping ui/*.yaml lowered specs. NOT diffed: `moduleExports`, the tree's INTERNAL export set — it is churned by ordinary refactoring and exists only so an `unexported` claim can be verified.

THE SELF-COMPARISON CAVEAT, stated rather than dodged. The original device warned that a baseline captured from the tree under test "passes unconditionally and proves nothing". That warning was about capturing from the BRANCH, and it is now enforced MECHANICALLY rather than by a pinned commit literal: capture-surface-baseline.test.mjs requires the fixture's commit to be an ANCESTOR OF MAIN (fail-closed — if no main ref resolves it fails rather than skipping) and to match the `baseline.commit` declared here. So a baseline captured from the branch under test is refused, whichever commit it is. On main itself the 0-difference reading is the LOCK HOLDING, not a tautology — change the surface and the count moves. The residual, named honestly: an author can still re-capture from a MERGED main that already carries their change. What stops that being silent is that re-capturing is a large, reviewable diff to a committed fixture plus an emptied manifest, not an edit to a threshold. The verification LOGIC no longer depends on this file's contents at all — `evaluate()` is unit-tested directly, which is what stopped disposition COUNTS in this file standing in for the logic they were meant to keep alive.

ATTRIBUTING A DIFFERENCE, mechanically, when this list is not empty. "Which population is this in?" is answered by RE-CAPTURING the same frozen baseline against the MERGE-BASE tree and set-differencing the two diff lists — not by reading `git status`. A file with no UNCOMMITTED change can still carry hundreds of lines of change in the branch's COMMITS. Recipe: `git archive <merge-base> | tar -x -C /tmp/mb`, symlink the repo `node_modules` into that tree, then `node scripts/capture-surface-baseline.mjs compare --baseline <frozen> --root /tmp/mb --json` and set-difference its `diffs[]` keys against the same run at HEAD. Compare PREFIXES as well as exact keys: `pointerDiff` reports the SHALLOWEST differing path, so a subtree main replaced wholesale would otherwise look unrelated to its own leaves. Two traps found the hard way: inserting a sibling widget RENUMBERS an index-based pointer, so first-appearance attribution misreads it; and a leaf's semantic change can be older than its current shape, because a leaf surfaces only once a sibling key appears beside it.

EDITING THIS FILE: it is 1-space-indent JSON that escapes EVERY ASCII hyphen as a \u002d escape (there are ZERO literal hyphens in it) while leaving other non-ASCII (— → … × Σ) literal. A json.loads/json.dumps round-trip cannot reproduce that and rewrites the whole file; two separate attempts did (1623/1161 and 4802/4361 lines of pure formatting churn). Edit it as TEXT: split the entries on the 2-space `{` / `}` boundaries, keep untouched blocks byte-identical, and render a new entry with JSON.stringify(entry, null, 1), indent every line by 2, THEN replace hyphens — escaping before stringify double-escapes the backslash and yields literal "\u002d" text instead of a hyphen.

expected.name: CATEGORY_DERIVATION_VERSION
expected.why: ITEM-36: the declared-level spelling bridge and the category-derivation version stamp. A producer declares bool levels lowercase while the comparator spells a JS boolean capitalised, so a raw declared level matches nothing and drops every row of a boolean criterion silently; spellDeclaredLevel is the bridge every declared level crosses before it is offered. CATEGORY_DERIVATION_VERSION stamps HOW the option set is derived, which CRITERIA_COERCION_VERSION does not cover: a keep-set persists by name, so changing the names on offer moves a saved criterion's answer with nothing to notice it. Additive; both are published on the barrel because the criteria contract is already a core public seam.

expected.name: asNumsNaNMissing
expected.why: the ONE column coercer (three copies of asNums/asStrs had drifted APART semantically: store.ts mapped a missing entry to NaN, the two canvas copies to 0). Consolidated into core/columns/columnCoerce.ts and published on the barrel for the same reason isIdentifierColumn is: both core and the canvas extension read a columnar value through it, and the layer lint refuses a deep import past the barrel. Additive only; nothing was removed and every call site keeps the semantics it had, which a test pins.

expected.name: cell-filter/widgets/#unreadableColumnsAlert
expected.detail: added: {"id":"unreadableColumnsAlert","kind":"alert","text":"This dataset's per-cell measurements are listed but could not be read, so there is nothing to build criteria on yet. They may still be uploading —
expected.why: the `unreadableColumnsAlert` alert is the authored sentence for the new `unreadable` data status, and this is the WHOLE of the difference it makes. Declared blanket because a widget's serialisation is longer than the 200 chars `detail` binds. Until ITEM-P1 this ONE difference cost 72 allowances: index-keyed array diffing renumbered all 11 later widgets plus the trailing element, and 71 of the 72 entries said nothing.

expected.name: qc/widgets/#metricTable/columns/3/cell/button/icon
expected.why: REPORTED: the per-row remove action should be an icon. `icon: remove` is a key into the renderer's closed row-action glyph registry; the vocabulary and the glyph both already existed and cell-filter's criteria table has read this way since it shipped, so this is the second table arriving at the same answer rather than a new capability. The declared `label` is not dropped — it stays the accessible name AND the hover tooltip, carrying the row with it. This is the WHOLE of the difference: one leaf key, at pointer depth 7, so no blanket permit.

expected.name: cell-filter/canvas/series/#s-emb-before/encode/colorBy
expected.why: REPORTED: choosing a Group by did not colour the projection panes. `VizColorBy` requires `{ mode, key }`; the view shipped a bare ref string, which `resolveColorBy` filled into a mode-less, key-less object that every consumer reads as "colour by nothing" — a control that looked wired and was a silent no-op. This is the WHOLE of the difference: one leaf key restated in the shape viz has always required, at pointer depth 6, so no blanket permit. Disposition `renamed` because the vocabulary has no value for a same-binding-corrected-spelling change, and `renamed` is the only one that does not claim the binding moved, went away, or is new. `parseOption` now REFUSES a key-less colorBy, so the old spelling can no longer ship unnoticed, and an unset key drops the channel (absence already means no colouring).

expected.name: flattenFields
expected.why: deleted as UNREACHABLE with the stepped/wizard form. Re-verified at deletion rather than inherited: `AnalysisRunPanel` is the ONLY host of `<SchemaForm>` in the tree; it always passes `fallbackParamsFor(analysis)`, a flat `{fields}` synthesised from `appliesTo` alone; `AnalysisContribution` has no `params` key at all (removed under INV-1); and `params` sits in the REJECTED-KEYS list in `core/runtime/loadProcessors.ts`, so a processor manifest declaring one FAILS TO LOAD. Processor `ui/*.yaml` are view_specs rendered by the declarative view engine and never construct a ParamsSchema. Restoration notes: `extensions/widgets/form/SchemaForm.tsx`. It reconciled `steps[].fields` with the top-level `fields[]`. With `steps` gone it is the identity function on `schema.fields`, so its call sites read `.fields` directly.

expected.name: cell-filter/inspects
expected.why: ITEM-68 removes the view_spec `inspects:` key. A key with no reader has no defined meaning, so the next reader would have been free to invent one and the two declarations could then disagree with nothing to arbitrate. Declared `blanket` ON PURPOSE: the change genuinely IS wholesale — a top-level key REMOVED from the spec, not an edit inside a subtree — which is exactly the case the depth rule asks to be named out loud.

expected.name: BINDING_ORIGIN_COPY
expected.why: the `binding-origin` vocabulary: how a binding was CHOSEN (`user` | `auto`), plus the fold that resolves it across several references and the one wording of its visible mark. It is exported from the `core` barrel rather than deep-imported because FOUR surfaces render or read it and they straddle the layer boundary — the declared `artifact_ref` widget and the pane anchor in `core`, the fallback form's control and the run panel in `extensions` — so the barrel is the only place all four can reach without a `deep-import-across-layer` violation. A literal per surface is the same fact waiting to drift into four slightly different claims, which is the shape of the defect this change exists to fix.

expected.name: onPaneClosed
expected.why: the pane CLOSE signal, the other half of the `usePaneStateValue` contract already on this barrel. A region renders only its ACTIVE tab, so a pane's unmount means the user looked away, not that the pane is done — and a pane can own a LIVE resource (a run's progress stream) that must survive that and end on CLOSE. `runSession.ts` subscribes to it so no pane host has to remember the teardown. Additive: `clearPaneState`'s existing behaviour is unchanged, the listener set is empty unless something subscribes.

expected.name: cell-filter/data/obs/args/values_for
expected.why: ITEM-34: `values_for` turns the axis_columns read LAZY — metadata for every column on the axis, VALUES only for the columns a criterion actually names. It is the read-reduction the item exists for (the reference dataset imports 65 columns, all of which were fetched to populate a picker that needs only names, kinds and levels). Additive and opt-in: a slice that omits it is byte-identical to the eager behaviour, which is why qc.yaml's axis_columns slice is untouched.

expected.name: cell-filter/derived/pendingColumns
expected.why: ITEM-34 / DRIFT-1.11: the LOADING GATE the owner chose (option 1, 2026-08-15) — gate the slice until every criterion-named body has arrived. `pending_criterion_columns` is the derived kernel that names WHICH criterion is waiting; it is the production caller that closes the last capability-without-a-consumer in this feature. It answers with column names rather than a boolean so a user with several criteria can tell which one is not ready. Declared `blanket` deliberately: this is a WHOLESALE addition — a derived entry / a widget that did not exist — so the permitted change genuinely is the entire element, not a field inside one.

expected.name: cell-filter/widgets/#pendingColumnsAlert

The mask is already all-FALSE while a criterion is pending (conservative and visible, never permissive and invisible); this alert is what makes that safety legible, naming the waiting column rather than showing a bare spinner, and sitting above the table so it is read before the result below it. Declared `blanket` deliberately: this is a WHOLESALE addition — a derived entry / a widget that did not exist — so the permitted change genuinely is the entire element, not a field inside one.

It exists because the declarative column_values slice and the canvas must read a column through ONE byte route: core may not import an extension (lint-layer-boundary R2), so the capability is the only conforming seam, and the read takes an artifact id plus the producer-declared structure.
